items.name: animated-price
items.title: Animated price
items.description: Currency-aware price transitions with the same soft count and blur across every price update.
items.docs: Data in, callbacks out. Locale defaults to en-US; pass your application locale explicitly. Reduced motion shows the final state immediately.

items.name: animated-price-demo
items.title: Animated price demo
items.description: An interactive example with real state changes and accessible controls.

items.name: product-card
items.title: Product card
items.description: A production product card for React and Next.js: image with hover zoom, sale and stock badges, compare-at price, colour swatches with radiogroup semantics, add to cart, and a matching skeleton.
items.docs: Pass a plain product object and handle onAddToCart; the card never fetches. Format prices before you pass them so the card stays locale-neutral. Use renderImage to plug in next/image.

items.name: product-card-demo
items.title: Product card demo
items.description: Two product cards: one on sale with colour variants, one sold out.

items.name: money
items.title: Money
items.description: Money in minor units with its currency, and the helpers every commerce item shares: format for a locale, sum and multiply without drift.

items.name: pay-button
items.title: Pay button
items.description: The checkout button with its whole life: the amount on it, locked until the form is valid, processing, the bank step, paid, and failed with a safe retry.
items.docs: Send every press's attempt id to your server as the idempotency key. Pass disabledReason while the form is invalid, status from your payment provider (or let the promise from onPay drive it), and call step.authenticating() when the bank asks for a confirmation. Inside a checkout form use type="submit".

items.name: pay-button-demo
items.title: Pay button demo
items.description: A working preview of Pay button.

items.name: product-tile
items.title: Product tile
items.description: A quiet product tile for editorial grids: one link, a picture that swaps on hover, the name and the price, with a skeleton and no buttons.
items.docs: Prices are minor units with a currency, and locale should always be passed so the price matches on the server and in the browser. The tile holds no button, so it is safe in a carousel; set priority on the first row and pass renderImage to use next/image. ProductTileSkeleton keeps the grid steady while data loads.

items.name: product-tile-demo
items.title: Product tile demo
items.description: A working preview of Product tile.

items.name: product-row-card
items.title: Product row card
items.description: A list-view product card for search results: picture, title, rating and facts, then the price block, stock in words and the actions.
items.docs: Prices are Money in minor units. The title is the stretched link; Add to cart and your wishlist control stay separate controls above it. onAddToCart may return a promise to show the busy state, and ProductRowCardSkeleton stands in while a list loads. On a phone the price block stacks above a full-width Add to cart that is 40px high, so give a wishlist control the same height.

items.name: product-row-card-demo
items.title: Product row card demo
items.description: A working preview of Product row card.

items.name: mini-product-row
items.title: Mini product row
items.description: A one-line product reference for suggestions, bundles and pickers: thumbnail, name, option and price, as a link, a button or a plain row.
items.docs: Give it href for a link or onClick for a button; with neither it is a plain row. trailing stays a separate control above the stretched link, so a checkbox or a remove button is safe. selected adds a check and aria-pressed (button) or aria-current (link).

items.name: mini-product-row-demo
items.title: Mini product row demo
items.description: A working preview of Mini product row.

items.name: base-price
items.title: Base price
items.description: The required price per 100 g or per litre, worked out from the pack size and price, converted, rounded half up and formatted for the locale.
items.docs: Pass the price of the pack in minor units, how much one pack holds and its unit; the base price is worked out here, rounded half up to the cent. Give it an id and point the price's aria-describedby at it. computeBasePrice is exported for sorting or analytics.

items.name: base-price-demo
items.title: Base price demo
items.description: A working preview of Base price.

items.name: price-range
items.title: Price range
items.description: A price for products with variants: 'From 19', '19 to 39' or one price, with sale ranges handled and struck through.
items.docs: min and max are minor units. variant="from" shows the lowest price after a word; variant="range" shows both ends with Intl formatRange. cents="auto" drops .00 when every figure is whole. The compare-at range is struck through only when it is higher.

items.name: price-range-demo
items.title: Price range demo
items.description: A working preview of Price range.

items.name: quantity-stepper
items.title: Quantity stepper
items.description: A quantity control for carts: minus, plus and a typed value, with pack steps, a stock cap, hold to repeat and remove at one.
items.docs: Controlled (value, onChange) or uncontrolled (defaultValue). min defaults to 1 and every value is min plus whole steps. stockLimit and max cap it; removeAtMin turns the minus into a trash button that calls onRemove. A press steps when it is released, so a scroll that starts on a button changes nothing; holding repeats, and neither a hold nor a key repeat ever removes the line. busy ignores presses and covers the number with a spinner without changing the size.

items.name: quantity-stepper-demo
items.title: Quantity stepper demo
items.description: A working preview of Quantity stepper.

items.name: add-to-cart-button
items.title: Add to cart button
items.description: The buy button with its commerce states: select an option, adding, added with View cart, failed with retry, sold out and pre-order.
items.docs: onAdd may return a promise: the button is busy until it settles, says Added beside a View cart link, or shows an inline error that retries. Pass missingOption while a variant is unchosen, soldOut with onNotify for Notify me, preorder for a ship date, or drive it with status.

items.name: add-to-cart-button-demo
items.title: Add to cart button demo
items.description: A working preview of Add to cart button.

items.name: product-info-tabs
items.title: Product info tabs
items.description: Description, details, shipping and reviews as tabs on desktop and an accordion on a phone, from the same content.
items.docs: Give every section a short id: the URL hash #id opens it, and the hash follows the open section. Closed panels stay in the document. Below the breakpoint (768 px by default) the sections become a single-open accordion whose headings use headingLevel. The server renders the tabs, so until the page is interactive a small inline style hides the tab row under the breakpoint and a phone never paints a row that does not fit (a strict style-src policy blocks that rule; the row then scrolls inside itself).

items.name: product-info-tabs-demo
items.title: Product info tabs demo
items.description: A working preview of Product info tabs.

items.name: fit-scale
items.title: Fit scale
items.description: Where an item runs, from small to large, as a five-point scale with the marker placed from review data.
items.docs: value is the average fit from 1 (runs small) to 5 (runs large). Without a value, or with a count of 0, it renders nothing. Pass labels for another language: the sentence uses {fit} and {count}.

items.name: fit-scale-demo
items.title: Fit scale demo
items.description: A working preview of Fit scale.

items.name: shipping-estimator
items.title: Shipping estimator
items.description: Country and postcode in, delivery options out: the cart's shipping estimator with prices, arrival windows and a postcode check per country.
items.docs: onEstimate gets a country and a postcode that already match the country's format, and returns the options: an empty list means you do not ship there, a rejection shows a retry message. Amounts are in minor units. Pass onSelect and the list becomes a radio group; it is called with null when the choice no longer stands (the country or postcode was edited, or a new estimate started), so clear whatever you stored. Pass defaultOptions to restore an earlier estimate. postcodes.ts exports the format rules, so the same check can run on your server.

items.name: shipping-estimator-demo
items.title: Shipping estimator demo
items.description: A working preview of Shipping estimator.

items.name: order-line
items.title: Order line
items.description: A read-only order line: picture, name, option, quantity times unit price, line total and a per-line status, read out as one sentence.
items.docs: Amounts are in minor units. compareAtAmount draws a struck price, discount adds a line and takes its amount off the total. Put lines in a <ul>; use as="div" outside a list. Pass statusLabel to translate the chip.

items.name: order-line-demo
items.title: Order line demo
items.description: A working preview of Order line.

items.name: order-card
items.title: Order card
items.description: An order in a customer's history: number, date, status, thumbnails, total and the next step as a button, with the whole card linking to the order.
items.docs: Dates are ISO strings, read in timeZone (UTC by default) and written out in locale. The action that fits the status is chosen for you (track, reorder); give order.actions to choose your own (up to three; the first is the main button, and on a compact card they wrap to a second line when the row is narrow). The buttons sit above a stretched link. Give an action an address with actionHrefs and it is a link that needs no JavaScript; for the others pass onAction from a client component.

items.name: order-card-demo
items.title: Order card demo
items.description: A working preview of Order card.

items.name: order-lookup
items.title: Order lookup
items.description: Where is my order? An order number and email form for guests, with answers that never reveal who has orders.
items.docs: onLookup resolves with whatever should appear under the form, or with null when nothing matches: a missing order and a wrong email give the same words. Reject for a failure on your side. The answer under the form goes away as soon as a field is edited. Rate-limit the endpoint behind it; the form cannot do that for you.

items.name: order-lookup-demo
items.title: Order lookup demo
items.description: A working preview of Order lookup.

items.name: modifier-group
items.title: Modifier group
items.description: Options with rules for products and menus: required, pick one or up to N, price add-ons and a polite count of what is chosen.
items.docs: max 1 (the default) draws radios, anything more draws checkboxes that lock at the maximum; pass Infinity for no limit. min of 1 or more marks the group Required. Prices are in minor units. The message for a missing choice shows after the first change, or at once with invalid.

items.name: modifier-group-demo
items.title: Modifier group demo
items.description: A working preview of Modifier group.

items.name: view-cart-bar
items.title: View cart bar
items.description: A bar pinned to the bottom with item count, total and a View cart button, rising when the first item is added and resting above the footer.
items.docs: It is sticky, not fixed: render it as the last child of your page's main content, and it stays on the bottom edge of the screen while you scroll, then rests above the footer. total is in minor units. Use hidden on the cart page itself.

items.name: view-cart-bar-demo
items.title: View cart bar demo
items.description: A working preview of View cart bar.

items.name: promo-tile
items.title: Promo tile
items.description: A promotional tile for a product grid: a picture, a short headline and one action, one or two columns wide, with words on a solid plate.
items.docs: Put it in a grid next to product cards and add grid-flow-dense to the grid, so a wide tile never leaves a gap. span={2} applies from the sm breakpoint up; on a phone every tile is one column, and it fits its own track whether the grid has one column there or two. The picture is decorative unless you give it alt text, and a screen reader hears "Promotion" first.

items.name: promo-tile-demo
items.title: Promo tile demo
items.description: A working preview of Promo tile.

items.name: cart-issues
items.title: Cart issues
items.description: The problems in a cart that need fixing before checkout: unavailable lines, price changes and minimums, each with its one fix.
items.docs: Remove an issue from the list when you have fixed it or the shopper has dismissed it, and keep the component mounted when the list is empty: focus moves to the next action, or to the status line when the last one is gone. Everything blocks except a price change, unless you set blocking. Point your checkout button's aria-describedby at the region's id, or print summarizeCartIssues(issues).reason (from cart-issues/issues, which also runs on the server) next to it. onBlockingChange reports the change.

items.name: cart-issues-demo
items.title: Cart issues demo
items.description: A working preview of Cart issues.

items.name: rating-inline
items.title: Rating inline
items.description: Stars drawn to the exact average, the score and the review count in one line, linking to the reviews, for product titles and cards.
items.docs: Give it the average and the count; a count of zero shows emptyText ("No reviews yet"), or nothing with emptyText={null}. With href the whole line is a link. Pass label to translate the sentence a screen reader hears. To collect a rating use the Rating primitive.

items.name: rating-inline-demo
items.title: Rating inline demo
items.description: A working preview of Rating inline.

items.name: add-stepper
items.title: Add stepper
items.description: An Add button that turns into minus, count and plus in the same footprint once something is in the cart, as in ordering apps.
items.docs: Controlled with value and onChange, or uncontrolled with defaultValue; zero means not in the cart. stockLimit and max disable plus and print the reason under the control, without taking room, so leave a line of space there; busy keeps the width and the focus while your cart updates. Minus at min removes the item. Always pass label: it is in every accessible name.

items.name: add-stepper-demo
items.title: Add stepper demo
items.description: A working preview of Add stepper.

items.name: sales-unit-picker
items.title: Sales unit picker
items.description: Let shoppers buy by the piece, the box, the pallet or by weight: every unit shows its price per piece, switching converts the quantity, and the total is worked out.
items.docs: Describe the product's units with pieces (how many pieces one holds) and price in minor units; the price per piece, the saving against the smallest pack and the conversion between units all come from those two numbers. A unit's min, step and max are its rules: quantities are multiples of step, at least min, at most max, and a typed number is corrected with a message. Switching unit works from the pieces the shopper asked for and rounds up, never down, so looking at the units never changes the order: switch back and the same quantity returns. Typing, stepping or pushing against a limit is what changes the ask. onChange always carries a quantity the rules allow plus the line total. With mode="weight" pass pricePerKilo and the amounts are grams. units.ts holds the arithmetic and runs on the server too.

items.name: sales-unit-picker-demo
items.title: Sales unit picker demo
items.description: A working preview of Sales unit picker.

items.name: quantity-calculator
items.title: Quantity calculator
items.description: Tell shoppers how many packs a job needs: enter an area or a length and width and a waste margin, and get whole packs rounded up, what they cover and the price.
items.docs: coveragePerPack is what one pack covers in unit (m2 or ft2); packPrice is in minor units and optional. The shopper types an area or a length and a width, and a waste margin that starts at wastePercent; a blank margin counts as wastePercent, as its placeholder says. Results always round up, and the panel says so. Typing 7,5 or 7.5 means the same, and 1,200 is read the way locale writes it. Every field has a message for a missing, unreadable, zero or too large number; maxArea is the largest believable area. onAddToCart receives the packs: return a promise and the button shows it is working, reject and the shopper is told. calculate.ts holds the arithmetic, counted in whole thousandths, and runs on the server too.

items.name: quantity-calculator-demo
items.title: Quantity calculator demo
items.description: A working preview of Quantity calculator.

items.name: compatibility-check
items.title: Compatibility check
items.description: Answer "will it fit?" for cases, filters and spare parts: pick a brand and a model and get compatible, not compatible with alternatives, or unknown, never a guess.
items.docs: Give it brands, models (each with the id of its brand) and the ids the product fits in compatible. Pass incompatible too when you know which models it does not fit: a model on neither list is then reported as unknown, instead of being guessed at. alternatives (by model id) are listed under a not-compatible answer, and contactHref adds an ask-us link to the unknown one. onCheck receives the brand, the model and the verdict whenever both are chosen: store that and pass it back as defaultValue to remember the last choice. productName is the subject of a sentence ("Halcyon MagGrip car mount fits the Orbit One."), so keep it singular or change the wording with labels. Until a brand is chosen the model field is disabled, and a line of text under it says why. fit.ts holds verdictFor and runs on the server too.

items.name: compatibility-check-demo
items.title: Compatibility check demo
items.description: A working preview of Compatibility check.

items.name: shoppable-list
items.title: Shoppable list
items.description: A recipe or project as a shopping list: amounts that scale with servings, substitutes for sold-out lines, and one button that adds the checked products to the cart.
items.docs: Each item is a product (id, name, price of one pack, optional packSize) with the amount the recipe needs for servings people. With servings the list gets a servings field and every amount scales, and so does the number of packs: 600 g needs two 500 g packs. A line with no amount (note: "to taste") is bought once. defaultChecked: false starts a line unchecked, for things the reader probably owns. A sold-out line (inStock: false) cannot be checked and offers its substitute; swapping checks it and onAddAll then carries the substitute's id. onAddAll receives only the checked lines, each with the product id, the packs, the price of one pack and the total; return a promise and the button shows it is working. list.ts holds the arithmetic and runs on the server too.

items.name: shoppable-list-demo
items.title: Shoppable list demo
items.description: A working preview of Shoppable list.

items.name: round-up-toggle
items.title: Round up toggle
items.description: Offer to round the order up to the next euro for a good cause: the exact extra amount and the cause are in the question, and the switch starts off.
items.docs: total and step are in minor units: 2457 with a step of 100 offers to round up by 43 to 2500. It is off until the shopper turns it on, so it never nudges; defaultChecked is for restoring their own earlier choice. onChange receives the new state and { amount, total }: add amount to the order as a donation while it is on. When the total is already a multiple of the step the component renders nothing, so treat the donation as zero. cause is in the question, always. round-up.ts holds roundUpOf, which runs on the server too, so the order you charge is computed the same way you showed it.

items.name: round-up-toggle-demo
items.title: Round up toggle demo
items.description: A working preview of Round up toggle.

items.name: installment-line
items.title: Installment line
items.description: The "or pay in 3 × 33.00" line under a price, with a popover for the schedule and terms: parts that add up exactly, fees stated, no provider logo.
items.docs: price and fee are in minor units. The parts are worked out so they always add up to price plus fee: what does not divide evenly goes on the first payment, and the line says so ("the first 37.52"). interval is week, two-weeks or month. Without now the details say how long after the first each payment is taken, which is the same on the server and in the browser; pass now (and timeZone) to give every payment its date. minPrice and maxPrice are the range you allow: outside it nothing is rendered. A fee of 0 says there is no fee; leave fee out to say nothing. terms is the small print. It has no state of its own, so it renders in a Server Component. installments.ts holds planInstallments and paymentDays, which run on the server too, so the schedule you charge is the one you showed.

items.name: installment-line-demo
items.title: Installment line demo
items.description: A working preview of Installment line.

items.name: return-window
items.title: Return window
items.description: Show how long an order can still be returned: the closing date, the days left, and open, closing soon and closed states, with Start return only while it is open.
items.docs: deliveredAt is an ISO date-time or a plain date such as "2026-10-20"; windowDays is how many days after the delivery day returns are accepted, so delivered 2 October with 30 days the last day is 1 November. Whole calendar days are counted in timeZone, which should be the shop's: the window closes at midnight there. Under soonDays (3) days left it is closing soon; on the last day it says so; the day after it is closed and the button goes. Pass now from the server for a first render that matches the browser; without it the first render shows only the date and the days appear once the browser's clock is read, so a cached page never claims days it cannot know. Start return is a button with onStartReturn, or a link with startReturnHref. window.ts holds the calendar arithmetic and runs on the server too, so you can refuse a late return there with the same rule.

items.name: return-window-demo
items.title: Return window demo
items.description: A working preview of Return window.

items.name: order-edit-window
items.title: Order edit window
items.description: Tell shoppers a fresh order can still be changed: the time left in words, actions to edit the address or items or cancel, and a calm swap when time is up.
items.docs: editableUntil is the moment the order stops being editable, with its offset ("2026-10-20T10:24:00Z"). The time is written in whole minutes, rounded down, and updates once a minute; only the 10 minute and 1 minute marks and the end are announced, politely, and never for where the time already stands when the page loads. At zero both sentences are laid in one cell, so the strip does not change size, the actions go aria-disabled (still focusable, so a keyboard user is not dropped), and onExpire is called once; never trust the browser for this, lock the order on your server as well. onAction receives address, items or cancel; cancel is only reported after the shopper confirms in the dialog, whose focus starts on Keep order. windowMinutes (optional) is the length of the whole window and adds a thin bar for how much is left. Pass now in tests and previews; without it the first render says "You can still change this order" and the time appears once the browser's clock is read. remaining.ts holds the arithmetic and runs on the server too.

items.name: order-edit-window-demo
items.title: Order edit window demo
items.description: A working preview of Order edit window.

items.name: courier-card
items.title: Courier card
items.description: The delivery driver at a glance: photo or initial, first name, vehicle and plate, rating and arrival time, with Call and Message buttons and a same-size waiting state.
items.docs: Pass the courier (a first name, and optionally photo, vehicle, plate, rating) and eta in minutes; send a new eta whenever your tracking has one. The card shows only the first word of the name and never draws a phone number: onCall and onMessage are buttons you handle, or callHref and messageHref make them links, in which case use a relay or masked number, since the href is in the page. Both are named for the courier ("Call Mehmet"). The visible arrival time follows every update; the spoken one waits for it to settle and only speaks when the state changes, the time moved by two minutes or more, or the courier is about to arrive. Without a courier (or with status="pending") the card keeps its size and says "Looking for a courier"; the buttons are there but disabled. status="arrived" ends the countdown. eta.ts holds firstName and the rule for what is worth saying, and runs on the server too.

items.name: courier-card-demo
items.title: Courier card demo
items.description: A working preview of Courier card.

items.name: kitchen-ticket
items.title: Kitchen ticket
items.description: A kitchen order ticket: number, order type, items with modifiers, an elapsed timer that escalates in words, allergies read first and a Bump button.
items.docs: Pass one clock as now to every ticket on the board (a number, a date or an ISO string), so they tick together and render the same on the server. thresholds sets in minutes when a ticket runs slow (default 8) and when it is late (default 12). Without status the ticket keeps its own open or bumped state; pass status and handle onBump and onRecall to control it from your list, and take the ticket off the screen yourself. Allergies are set apart in an inverted block and come first in the reading order. A bumped ticket stops its timer at order.bumpedAt, or at the moment of the bump. labels holds every word, for another language.

items.name: kitchen-ticket-demo
items.title: Kitchen ticket demo
items.description: A working preview of Kitchen ticket.

items.name: bank-transfer-details
items.title: Bank transfer details
items.description: How to pay by bank transfer: beneficiary, IBAN, BIC, the exact amount and the reference, each with a copy button, and the deadline.
items.docs: details (a BankTransferAccount) holds the account: beneficiary, iban, an optional bic, amount in minor units and the reference. The IBAN is shown in groups of four and copied without spaces, the amount is copied without a symbol and with the decimal mark of locale, and the reference is copied exactly as given. onCopy receives the row ("iban") and the text that reached the clipboard. deadline is when the order lapses, written in timeZone; pass now from the server and a deadline that has passed turns the buttons off and says so at the top of the card, in place of the instructions. Without now nothing is ever shown as lapsed. In a card narrower than 26rem the copy buttons are only their icon (still named Copy IBAN), so an account number keeps one line. labels holds every word, for another language.

items.name: bank-transfer-details-demo
items.title: Bank transfer details demo
items.description: A working preview of Bank transfer details.

items.name: seller-card
items.title: Seller card
items.description: Who sells this: name, verification in words, rating, items sold, reply time and member since, with Contact and Visit store as separate actions.
items.docs: Pass the seller as data: name, an optional logo (initials are drawn without one), verified, rating with reviews, itemsSold, replyMinutes and memberSince as an ISO date. What is missing is left out; a seller with no sales and no reviews shows New seller, and a rating is only shown with a review count above zero. The rating is the inline rating, so it says the same sentence to a screen reader. Contact is a button (onContact) or, with contactHref, a link; Visit store appears when you pass storeHref. The figures sit in a row once the card is wide enough and in a list when it is not, whatever the screen. compact is the smaller card for beside the price; a long name wraps to two lines and is in the title of the heading. Always pass locale so the numbers and the date match on the server and in the browser; a bare memberSince date is a calendar day and ignores timeZone. labels holds every word.

items.name: seller-card-demo
items.title: Seller card demo
items.description: A working preview of Seller card.

items.name: care-instructions
items.title: Care instructions
items.description: Garment care as a row of drawn symbols, each with its meaning in words: wash, bleach, tumble dry, dry, iron and professional care.
items.docs: care is an object of settings: wash ("95", "60", "50", "40", "30", "hand", "no"), bleach, tumbleDry, dry, iron and dryClean. Leave one out, or pass a value that is not known, and it is skipped, never drawn as something close; with nothing to show it renders nothing. layout="row" puts the words under each symbol, layout="list" beside it. showLabels={false} gives a row of bare symbols that are focusable and say their instruction in a tooltip and to a screen reader. labels replaces the words by key, for example { "wash-30": "Wasmachine, max 30 degrees" }.

items.name: care-instructions-demo
items.title: Care instructions demo
items.description: A working preview of Care instructions.

items.name: grade-scale
items.title: Grade scale
items.description: A letter-grade scale such as an energy class or eco score: the whole range drawn, steps that differ in length, the product's grade enlarged.
items.docs: grades runs from the best grade to the worst, so the first step is the shortest bar and the last the longest. value must be one of them: anything else draws the scale without a marker and the sentence says the product is not graded. label names what is graded and starts the sentence a screen reader hears. It draws a scale, not an official label: bring certified data to it.

items.name: grade-scale-demo
items.title: Grade scale demo
items.description: A working preview of Grade scale.

items.name: order-matrix
items.title: Order matrix
items.description: Order a product by size and colour in one grid: a quantity field per cell, stock hints, row and column totals, and paste from a spreadsheet.
items.docs: rows are the variants (colours or widths, with an optional swatch) and columns the sizes. stock holds what can be ordered per row id and column id: a cell that is missing is not made in that size and is disabled (a dash), zero is sold out and says Sold out under the field, and a quantity is held to its stock and said so; with lowStockAt or fewer left a cell says how many. Control the quantities with value and onChange or leave them to defaultValue; a cell at zero is left out of the object. minPerCell flags a quantity above zero but below the minimum and keeps Add from being pressed. unitPrice (minor units) adds the money. onAddAll receives every line and the totals and may return a promise. Arrow keys and Enter move between cells, and pasting a block of numbers from a spreadsheet fills the grid from the cell you are in. A grid wider than its frame scrolls sideways, keeps its first column in view (the field the keyboard moves to is scrolled clear of that column) and says so under the grid. Every field is named Navy, size M; labels holds every word, including the name pattern. Always pass locale.

items.name: order-matrix-demo
items.title: Order matrix demo
items.description: A working preview of Order matrix.

items.name: shipment-group
items.title: Shipment group
items.description: Items grouped by shipment: where it ships from, the delivery method and window, a status, then the lines that travel in that parcel.
items.docs: Pass the shipment (where it ships from, the delivery method with its price in minor units and an arrival window as ISO dates, and kind and shipsOn for a pre-order or a backorder), index and total, a status and the lines as children. Give each line its own vertical padding: the group draws the rules between them. With total of 1 the heading is dropped and only the delivery and the lines remain. status writes a badge that follows the shipment from Not shipped yet to Delivered, Delayed or Cancelled, and the card follows it: a delivered shipment says Arrived (pass the day it came as method.from), a cancelled one says nothing is on its way and mutes its price and lines, and a pre-order or backorder only says when it ships until it has left. Change is a button (onChangeMethod) or, with changeHref, a link, and it is only offered while the method can still change: not once the shipment is shipped, out for delivery, delivered or cancelled. Pass canChange to decide yourself. The group is a labelled region named by its heading. Always pass locale; a bare ISO date is a calendar day and ignores timeZone. labels holds every word.

items.name: dimension-diagram
items.title: Dimension diagram
items.description: Product dimensions drawn as a simple box, cylinder or flat shape with width, height and depth labelled, switchable between cm and inches.
items.docs: width, height and depth are in unit (centimetres by default); a cylinder takes its diameter as width, and without a depth the drawing is a flat elevation. The drawing scales to its container and the labels keep their size; when the drawing is small or the product narrow, the width label drops just below its line so the arrows stay in sight, and a label on the object gives up its name and keeps its figure (the names are always in the text above the drawing). A switch converts between the units in units and rounds the way a shop writes it (80 cm is 31.5 in); keep the choice yourself with displayUnit and onDisplayUnitChange so one switch can drive every diagram on the page, or leave it to defaultDisplayUnit. extras adds measurements such as { label: "Seat height", value: 46 } as a dashed line across the drawing. The same numbers are written above the drawing and as one sentence for a screen reader. Always pass locale.

items.name: refund-tracker
items.title: Refund tracker
items.description: Where a refund is: requested, received, approved and paid out, with dates, the amount and the expected arrival once it is approved.
items.docs: refund holds the amount in minor units, where it goes, and steps: an ISO date for each step that has happened (requested, received, approved, paid). The latest step with a date is the current one; steps before it count as done. expectedBy is shown only once the refund is approved, and without it the item says Usually 3 to 5 working days after approval. Pass now from the server and a date that has passed is called late. refund.issue explains a failed refund (it stops at its step and shows reason and action) or a partial one (refunded is the amount that is paid). Always pass locale; labels holds every word, for another language.
